Commentary.Commentary: Bangladesh with the depth in their batting would fancy themselves to chase this score down. The surface is a little slow, so if the Irish bowlers hit the right areas it might get a little difficult for the visitors. The game is in favour of the away side at the moment. Can the hosts spring a surprise? Join us in a while for the chase to find out.

The hosts never really going apart from the stand between Niall O'Brien and Ed Joyce which steadied their ship only for a while. Once the southphaw departed, they lost 3 wickets in quick succession and lost the plot. Dockrell and McCarthy helped them crawl their way to 181.

After being 116-3, Ireland have been bundled out for 181. Bangladesh after winning the toss and electing to bowl first will be happy with their effort. Mustafizur was the standout with 4 wickets in his 9 overs. Bangladesh were always  in control of the game as they were picking  wickets at regular intervals. They never let Ireland score freely.

The players are out in the middle. The two openers for Ireland are Ed Joyce and Paul Stirling. Bangladesh begin with Rubel Hossain! Two slips in place for him. Here we go...
Ireland XI - William Porterfield(c), Paul Stirling, Ed Joyce, Niall O'Brien (wk), Andrew Balbirnie, Kevin O'Brien, Gary Wilson, George Dockrell, Barry McCarthy, Tim Murtagh, Peter Chase.

Bangladesh XI - Tamim Iqbal, Soumya Sarkar, Sabbir Rahman, Mushfiqur Rahim (wk), Shakib Al Hasan, Mahmudullah, Mosaddek Hossain Saikat, Sunzamul Islam, Mashrafe Mortaza(c), Rubel Hossain, Mustafizur Rahman.

TOSS - Bangladesh win the toss and opt to field. Both teams have made a change each. SUNZAMUL ISLAM to make his ODI debut for Bangladesh, in place of Mehedi Hasan. Ireland bring in ED JOYCE for Simi Singh.

Pitch Report - There is more grass on the wicket than the last game. There should be more lateral movement with the new ball. 270-280 should be a good score on this wicket. The team winning the toss would like to have a bowl first.

Hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of Game 4 of the tri-series between Ireland and Bangladesh at The Village, Dublin. Both teams shared points the last time they met in the tournament and will hope for a better weather. The two teams in action today are yet to win a game and will be eager to get off the mark in that sense. Both teams are evenly matched with better bowling resources. If the  weather does not play spoilsport, we should have a close game! Stay tuned for all the details from the toss.
